title: Encrypted history store (blob storage of ciphertext frames)
goal: Durable, encrypted-at-rest storage and retrieval of per-session ciphertext frame history, served through GET/DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/history, with retention metadata and no ability to read content.
scope_in: History writer that receives each sequenced frame from the relay (header fields plus raw ct JSON) and appends it to batched blob objects in S3-compatible storage.
Index table with exactly the fields the contract allows: seq, id, from, ts, kind-class (event|queue|control), size, kid, blob key.
GET /v1/sessions/{id}/history?after_seq&limit paginated per CT-PAGE, returning ciphertext frames in seq order.
DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/history for host or workspace owner: purge blobs and index, write audit event.
Retention metadata (expires_at derived from entitlement history_days at session end) for the retention job to act on.
Blob storage adapter interface with S3/R2 and in-memory implementations.
scope_out: Hot buffer and WS replay: B042.
Retention purge scheduling and downgrade notice: B090.
Producing ciphertext, signing or any decryption: client side (CT-CRYPTO).
build_against: In-memory BlobStore fake and Postgres container; frames come from contracts/fixtures/envelope/ and contracts/fixtures/events/ (encrypted samples) or the B011 simulator. Authorisation via fake membership port.
interfaces: HistoryStore.append(sid: SessionId, frames: StoredFrame[]): Promise<{lastSeq: number}>  // idempotent on (sid, seq)
StoredFrame = {seq:number, id:'msg_…', from:'mem_…', ts:string, kindClass:'event'|'queue'|'control', size:number, kid:string|null, ct:CtObject|null, p:object|null}
HistoryStore.read(sid, afterSeq: number, limit: number): Promise<{frames: StoredFrame[], nextAfterSeq: number|null}>
BlobStore { put(key: string, body: Uint8Array, opts?): Promise<void>; get(key): Promise<Uint8Array>; delete(keys: string[]): Promise<void> }
Table history_index(session_id, seq, msg_id, member_id, ts, kind_class, size, kid, blob_key, pk(session_id,seq)); blob key pattern history/{sid}/{seq_start}-{seq_end}.bin
acceptance: Appending 1 000 frames then GET after_seq=0&limit=200 returns frames 1..200 in order, next_cursor set, and following the cursor 5 times returns all 1 000 with no gap or duplicate.

Appending the same (sid, seq) twice stores one row; appending seq 5 when 4 is missing is accepted but read reports a gap-free range only from contiguous data and exposes `from_seq` of earliest retained frame.
A viewer, editor and host of the session may GET history; a non-participant gets 404; a share-link guest token (B068) is a viewer and may read only when session policy share_history is true.
DELETE as editor returns 403; as host or workspace owner returns 204, subsequent GET returns an empty page, blob store lists zero keys for the session, and one audit event is written.
The history_index table has no column for text, paths, or p payload bodies of encrypted kinds; a schema test fails if a column outside the allowed list is added.
For hybrid frames only the cleartext p object defined by the contract is persisted alongside ct; for clear-kind frames p is persisted; `presence` frames are never passed to or stored by append.
Blob batches are written at most 2 s or 500 frames after the first frame in the batch; a crash between batch flush and index insert is repaired on restart without duplicate index rows.
GET returns ct unchanged byte-for-byte compared with what was appended (round trip test over 100 random binary-ish base64url values).
tests: history.authz.test.ts: role matrix and share_history policy
history.privacy.test.ts: schema column allow-list and log scrubbing (no ct in logs)
history.crash-recovery.test.ts: batch flush vs index insert
history.blobstore.contract.test.ts: same suite against memory and S3-compatible (minio container) implementations
guardrails: MUST treat ct as opaque bytes: never decode, decrypt, truncate or normalise it, and never log it.
MUST NOT store plaintext message text, paths or branch names; reject (and alert) any frame whose kind is encrypted but carries a non-empty p.
MUST NOT store ephemeral frames (presence, ping) or sys.* frames.
Blob object keys MUST NOT contain user-provided strings; only sid and numeric seq.
Purge MUST delete blobs before index rows so a failed purge can be retried and never leaves unreachable blobs.
Server-side encryption at rest MUST be enabled on the bucket; documented in README.
failure_modes: Blob store put fails -> retry with backoff + jitter (max 5), keep frames in the relay hot buffer, raise a metric/alert; do not ack durability to the relay until stored.
Blob get fails on read -> 503 with retry_after_s; partial page is never returned.
Purge partially fails -> response 202-style retry via job; GET during purge returns only frames not yet deleted and the purge is resumable.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: the history response frame shape reuses the envelope (CT-WS-ENVELOPE) but the OpenAPI document is not yet in contracts/, so item shape is the envelope minus nothing. Whether guests may read history is not stated; this lane gates it on share_history. Deliverable migration prefix 0055 = lane number.
